page.layout: One block of text: a running head at the top, then the title, two verse stanzas with headings, and a catchword at the lower right. No margin notes.

main_text.head: IOANNIS CALVINI, GENEuenfis Ecclefiaftæ, folidiffimæ erudi tionis, iudicij acutiffimi, indefeffi in vera pietate longè latéque propagandæ athletæ, innocentifs. vitæ fimplicitate in ipfa quoque morte & fepultura, teftata laudatiffimi, Memoriæ.

p.i: ROma ruentis terror ille maximus, Quem mortuum lugent boni, horrescùt mali. Ipfa a quo potuit Virtutem discere Virtus, Cur adeo exiguo, ignotóque in cespite clausus Caluinus lateat rogas? Caluinum assidue comitata modestia vivum, Hoc tumulo manibus condidit ipsa suis. O te beatum cespitem tanto hospite! O cui inuidere cuncta possint marmora!

main_text.head: EIDEM.

p.i: TE vivo, Caluine, fuit mihi vivere dulce, Hei, quàm dulce foret, te moriente, mori! Et tamen est, fateor, grata hoc mihi nomine vita, Quod tibi quas fundam sufficiat lacrymas. Vive igitur, Beza, in luctus, tibi ut vsque perenes Caluini in tumulum vita ministret aquas: Iunctura absenti donec te rursus amico, Mors pariter vitam finiat & lacrymas.

page.notes: The large initials R (of "Roma") and T (of "TE") are drop caps; read as ROma and TE. Some long-s and u/v forms were normalised as the rules require. Lines with a broken or unclear letter were read from the scan with best effort; no [?] marks were needed on clear words. The catchword EX sits alone at the lower right.
